newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia's Inkombank plans ADR issue.
newsitem.headline: Russia's Inkombank plans ADR issue.

text.p: Inkombank plans to issue level-one American Depositary Receipts (ADRs) in New York by the end of this year, an Inkombank official said on Thursday.
Bank of New York will be the depositary bank, and ING Bank Euroasia will handle custodian services in Russia, he said.
The bank intends to issue level-two or level-three ADRs in 1997 or 1998, he added.

The bank has already received permission from the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission to issue level-one ADRs, which allow investors in the U.S. to trade shares of a foreign company while avoiding its domestic settlement problems.
This can broaden the circle of shareholders, but does not raise new capital, which is only possible through level-two or level-three ADRs. These in turn have stricter requirements.
Russian banks require central bank permission to issue ADRs. Shares in Inkombank, as with other Russian banks, are rarely traded.
KPMG is auditing Inkombank's last three years of figures to international standards.
